claims.text: The local source slice models two ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign phase 1 rows: Articuno row 106 and Flying Pikachu row 107.

Bulbapedia's Articuno and Flying Pikachu card pages say the campaign ran between June 1 and July 31, 1999, and passengers could redeem two domestic boarding-pass stubs for a two-card set that included Articuno and Flying Pikachu.
Bulbapedia's Articuno page says the boarding-pass stubs had to be affixed to special postcards and mailed to Media Factory.
Bulbapedia credits the Japanese ANA Articuno artwork to Toshinao Aoki, and the Flying Pikachu page credits Flying Pikachu to Toshinao Aoki.
This source group matters because airline travel is not background flavor: the cards were acquired through flight evidence, postcards, and Media Factory, so route is part of identity.

narrative.human_title: ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign phase 1 — boarding passes become card provenance
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the cleanest examples of why the catalog has to care about assembly. The cards are not only Articuno and Flying Pikachu. They are a flight, two domestic boarding-pass stubs, a special postcard, Media Factory, and the little thrill of Pokemon leaving the binder for an airport counter. Flying Pikachu makes the route literal; Articuno gives it legendary sky weight. The result is beautiful and fragile for agents: the same names and artwork drift through CoroCoro, Wizards, Pokemon Web, Supreme Victors, Rising Rivals, and later air-travel Pikachu projects. The airline route is the spine.

narrative.human_title: Articuno — a legendary bird earned by flying
narrative.why_it_matters: Articuno is almost too elegant for this campaign. A legendary bird, obtained through airline travel, with boarding-pass stubs becoming the evidence that let the card enter your life. Toshinao Aoki's art later echoes through other prints, and the combined legendary-bird illustration makes the card feel bigger than a single promo. That is exactly why the route has to stay attached: ANA phase 1, two-card set, postcard to Media Factory, row 106.

narrative.human_title: Flying Pikachu — the flight record becomes the joke and the proof
narrative.why_it_matters: Flying Pikachu is charming because it is so literal. The card is Pikachu in the sky, and the campaign asked for proof that you had been in the sky too. Two boarding-pass stubs, a postcard, Media Factory, and then this tiny impossible Pikachu. That simplicity is also the trap: Flying Pikachu has many routes, from CoroCoro to Wizards to Game Boy sprites to later retro prints. The ANA phase 1 card is not just a Pikachu with balloons. It is the airline version, row 107, paired with Articuno.
